topic_ko: 지구의 공전이 365.2421일이므로 윤일을 더해 달력과 계절·행사를 제자리에 묶어 둔다

passage: Once in every four years February is handed a twenty-ninth day.
That extra square on the calendar is called Leap Day.
Its purpose is to keep the months we count and the seasons we live through pointing at the same thing.
A year feels like a tidy 365 days, yet the true circuit of Earth around the sun takes about 365.2421 days.
The leftover quarter of a day has to be repaid, and four years of it make one whole day.
Skip that repayment and winter would slide earlier and earlier through the calendar year.
Farmers planting by the calendar would meet frost too soon, and harvests would fail.
Festivals tied to a season or a date would drift away from the moment they were meant to mark.
choices: why an extra day must be added to keep the calendar matched to the seasons
how ancient astronomers first measured the length of a solar year
the customs that different countries observe on the twenty-ninth of February
the reason February is shorter than every other month of the year
how crop failures have shaped the history of farming communities
theme.explanation_ko: 365.2421일이라는 실제 공전 주기 때문에 하루를 더해 달력과 계절을 맞춘다는 것이 글 전체의 초점이므로 ①이 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ② 고대 천문학의 측정사는 언급이 없다. ③ 나라별 풍습은 다루지 않는다. ④ 2월이 짧은 이유는 설명되지 않는다. ⑤ 흉작은 결과의 한 예시일 뿐이다.

passage: Every fourth February receives one additional day, known as Leap Day.
It exists so that our calendar and the seasons never fall out of step.
We treat a year as 365 days, but Earth actually needs about 365.2421 days to circle the sun.
Those extra hours pile up, and every four years they amount to a full day that must be added back.
Without that correction, winter would arrive earlier and earlier on the calendar.
Agricultural schedules built around dates would fail, and crops could be lost.
Holidays and cultural celebrations are also tied to particular seasons or dates.
Left uncorrected, those events would slowly wander away from the times they were meant to honor.
choices: 윤일은 달력을 실제 공전 주기에 맞추어 계절과 행사가 어긋나지 않게 한다.
농업 일정은 달력보다 기후 관측에 근거해 세우는 것이 안전하다.
2월에 하루를 더하는 관습은 나라마다 서로 다르게 발전해 왔다.
지구의 공전 주기는 해마다 조금씩 길어지고 있어 조정이 필요하다.
명절의 날짜를 고정하면 문화 행사의 의미가 더 잘 보존된다.
gist.explanation_ko: 365.2421일이라는 실제 주기와 365일 달력의 차이를 윤일로 메워 계절·농사·행사가 제자리를 지키게 한다는 것이 요지이므로 ①이 적절하다.
gist.distractor_ko: ② 기후 관측을 권하는 글이 아니다. ③ 나라별 차이는 언급이 없다. ④ 공전 주기가 길어진다는 서술은 없다. ⑤ 날짜 고정이 아니라 달력 보정이 해법이다.

passage: A calendar is a promise that the same date will bring the same weather.
Keeping that promise takes an odd bit of bookkeeping every four years.
The trouble is that Earth does not orbit the sun in a neat 365 days.
It needs roughly 365.2421, and that fraction cannot simply be ignored.
So a twenty-ninth day is written into February once every four years.
Without it, winter would creep forward in the calendar year and confuse the planting season.
Crops sown by the wrong date could fail altogether.
Holidays fixed to a season would slowly drift from the time they were meant to celebrate.
choices: One Extra Day That Holds the Seasons in Place
February: The Strangest Month in History
Farming Without a Calendar: An Ancient Skill
How Fast Does the Earth Really Travel?
Festivals Around the World and Their Origins
title.explanation_ko: 하루의 추가가 계절을 제자리에 붙들어 둔다는 것이 글의 핵심이므로 ①이 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ② 2월의 역사를 다루지 않는다. ③ 달력 없는 농사는 논점이 아니다. ④ 공전 속도 자체가 주제는 아니다. ⑤ 축제의 기원은 언급이 없다.

passage: Every four years, a twenty-ninth day is added to February.
This day, called Leap Day, keeps our calendar and our seasons in line with each other.
A year seems to hold 365 days, but Earth takes about 365.2421 days to orbit the sun.
Holidays and cultural celebrations are often tied to a specific season or date.
Without leap years to keep the calendar in check, these events would gradually drift away from their intended time of celebration.
A harvest festival could slowly slide toward the middle of summer.
Winter itself would occur earlier in the calendar year.
Agricultural schedules would suffer, and crops could fail.
implication.underlined: Without leap years to keep the calendar in check, these events would gradually drift away from their intended time of celebration.
choices: Festivals would slowly fall on dates that no longer match their original season.
People would eventually forget why their festivals had been created.
Celebrations would have to be canceled once the calendar became inaccurate.
Each country would begin marking its holidays on a different day.
Holidays would gradually be replaced by newer, more popular events.
implication.explanation_ko: 달력이 어긋나면 행사 날짜가 본래의 계절에서 서서히 벗어난다는 뜻이므로 ①이 적절하다.
implication.distractor_ko: ② 기원을 잊는다는 내용이 아니다. ③ 행사 취소는 언급이 없다. ④ 나라별로 날짜가 달라진다는 뜻이 아니다. ⑤ 새로운 행사로 대체된다는 말은 없다.

passage: Once in every four years, February is given a twenty-ninth day.
That day, also known as Leap Day, exists to ensure that our calendar and our seasons keep in step with each other.
We picture a normal year as 365 days, yet it actually takes Earth about 365.2421 days to orbit the sun.
So once every four years an extra day must be added to account for the lost time.
Without the addition of a leap day, winter will occur earlier in the calendar year, causing problems for agricultural schedules.
Such a shift could potentially lead to crop failures across whole regions.
Besides that, countless holidays and cultural celebrations are linked to specific seasons or dates.
Without leap years to keep the calendar in check, these events would gradually drift away from their intended time.

grammar.explanation_ko: Without ~ 는 현재 사실의 반대를 가정하는 가정법 표현이므로 주절의 동사는 「조동사 과거형 + 동사원형」인 would occur 가 되어야 한다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ① 앞의 That day 를 부연하는 과거분사구로 적절하다. ② 「it takes + 사람/사물 + 시간 + to V」 구문의 정상 형태이다. ④ 앞 절 전체를 결과로 잇는 분사구문이다. ⑤ 행사가 계절과 '연관되는' 대상이므로 수동태가 옳다.

vocab.explanation_ko: 윤년이 없으면 행사들이 본래 시기에 '자리 잡는' 것이 아니라 그 시기에서 '점차 멀어질' 것이므로 settle into 는 drift away from 이 되어야 한다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ① 달력과 계절이 어긋나지 않도록 '보장한다'는 의미로 적절하다. ② 잃어버린 시간을 '메운다'는 뜻으로 옳다. ③ 농사 일정이 어긋난 결과인 '흉작'으로 자연스럽다. ④ '특정한' 계절이나 날짜와 연관된다는 서술로 알맞다.

passage: We speak of a year as 365 days, and for everyday purposes that is close enough.
Earth, however, keeps its own schedule and needs about 365.2421 days to finish one orbit.
Each year we therefore fall almost a quarter of a day behind the sky.
Four such years add up to a full day that has to be paid back at once.
That payment is Leap Day, the twenty-ninth of February.
Without it, winter would arrive earlier in the calendar year and ruin planting schedules.
Festivals fixed to a season would drift from the moment they were meant to mark.
choices: settle a debt the calendar owes to the sky each year
give farmers one additional day of rest before spring
make February as long as the other winter months
mark the exact moment when the Earth begins a new orbit
remind people that time cannot be measured precisely

passage: February gains a twenty-ninth day once every four years.

summary.summary_template: Because Earth's orbit is slightly __(A)__ than 365 days, a leap day is added every four years to stop the calendar from __(B)__ away from the seasons.
summary.explanation_ko: 공전 주기가 365일보다 약간 '길기' 때문에 달력이 계절에서 '멀어지는' 것을 막으려고 윤일을 더하므로 longer–drifting 이 적절하다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 지구가 태양의 궤도를 도는 데는 실제로 약 365.2421일이 걸린다.
writing.answer: It actually takes Earth about 365.2421 days to orbit the sun.
writing.explanation_ko: 「it takes + 대상 + 시간 + to V」 구문으로, it 은 가주어가 아니라 시간을 나타내는 비인칭 주어이다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 우리말을 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 윤일의 추가가 없다면, 겨울이 달력상의 한 해에서 더 일찍 찾아올 것이다.
conditions: the addition of a leap day 를 사용할 것
writing.answer: Without the addition of a leap day, winter would occur earlier in the calendar year.
writing.explanation_ko: Without 은 현재 사실의 반대를 가정하므로 주절에 「would + 동사원형」을 쓴다.

writing.question: 본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸에 알맞은 한 단어를 쓰시오.
writing.context: An extra day is added every four years to ___________ for the time that would otherwise be lost from the calendar.
writing.explanation_ko: 본문의 account for(~을 메우다, 설명하다)를 그대로 쓰면 된다.

writing.question: 다음 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: Without the addition of a leap day, winter would occur earlier in the calendar year, causing problems for agricultural schedules and potentially leading to crop failures.
writing.answer: 윤일의 추가가 없다면, 겨울이 달력상의 한 해에서 더 일찍 찾아와 농업 일정에 문제를 일으키고 잠재적으로 흉작으로 이어질 것이다.
writing.explanation_ko: Without 은 가정법을 이끌고, causing 과 leading 은 앞 절 전체를 결과로 잇는 병렬 분사구문이다.

writing.question: 본문을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Leap Day keeps our calendar and our __(A)__ in line, so that holidays do not gradually __(B)__ away from their intended time.
writing.explanation_ko: 본문에서 윤일은 calendar 와 seasons 를 in line 으로 유지하며, 행사들이 drift away 하는 것을 막는다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 이 글의 주제문을 영어로 쓰시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 쓰시오.
conditions: leap day 와 seasons 를 반드시 포함할 것
writing.answer: A leap day is added every four years to keep the calendar matching the seasons.
writing.explanation_ko: 4년마다 하루를 더하는 이유가 달력과 계절의 일치임을 한 문장으로 담으면 된다.
